iterations.theme: Duhovnost sv. Atanazija Velikog: obrana nicejskog pravovjerja, teologija pobožanstvenjenja i poticaj monaštvu

sections.subtitle: Četvrto stoljeće: vrijeme kada je Duh Sveti podigao velikane
sections.screenshot_description: Don Mladen Parlov uvodi gledatelje u 4. stoljeće i najavljuje velike crkvene oce
sections.content:
Podcast „Na krilima Duha“, koji se emitira u okviru **Mreža Riječi**, u jedanaestoj je epizodi stigao do 4. stoljeća. Don Mladen Parlov epizodu otvara pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija“ i odmah ističe da je riječ o razdoblju **velikih, presudnih događaja** za život Crkve u cjelini. Ti će događaji, kako naglašava, obilježiti kršćanstvo i na istoku i na zapadu.

Voditelj sa zahvalnošću primjećuje da je upravo u tom stoljeću Duh Sveti podigao „gigante kršćanske misli i kršćanske vjere“. Nekolicina njih ponijela je i počasni naslov **„Veliki“**. Don Mladen Parlov najavljuje da će gotovo sve te velikane obraditi u podcastu, jer to zaslužuju, tim više što od većine njih postoji prijevod barem jednog djela na hrvatski jezik.

Među imenima koja nabraja su:
- **kapadočki oci** na istoku,
- **sveti Ambrozije** na zapadu,
- **sveti Atanazije** na istoku,
- **Hilarije** i brojni drugi autori.

Hod kroz 4. stoljeće započinje s prvim od velikana koji su ponijeli naslov „Veliki“, svetim Atanazijem. Don Mladen Parlov podsjeća da se on ubraja među **četiri velika istočna crkvena oca**.
sections.subtitle_en: The Fourth Century: A Time When the Holy Spirit Raised Up Giants
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Mladen Parlov introduces viewers to the 4th century and announces the great Church Fathers
sections.content_en:
The podcast “Na krilima Duha”, which is broadcast within **Mreža Riječi**, has in its eleventh episode reached the 4th century. Don Mladen Parlov opens the episode with the greeting “Praised be Jesus and Mary” and immediately emphasizes that this is a period of **great, decisive events** for the life of the Church as a whole. These events, as he stresses, will mark Christianity in both the East and the West.

The host gratefully notes that it was precisely in that century that the Holy Spirit raised up “giants of Christian thought and Christian faith”. A few of them also bore the honorary title **“the Great”**. Don Mladen Parlov announces that he will cover almost all these giants in the podcast, because they deserve it, all the more so because a translation of at least one work into Croatian exists for most of them.

Among the names he lists are:
- the **Cappadocian Fathers** in the East,
- **Saint Ambrose** in the West,
- **Saint Athanasius** in the East,
- **Hilary** and numerous other authors.

The walk through the 4th century begins with the first of the giants who bore the title “the Great”, Saint Athanasius. Don Mladen Parlov recalls that he is counted among the **four great Eastern Church Fathers**.

sections.subtitle: Dijete Aleksandrije i njezine teološke škole
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o rođenju sv. Atanazija u Aleksandriji
sections.content:
Atanazije je rođen u **Aleksandriji između 295. i 298. godine**. Don Mladen Parlov objašnjava da je Aleksandrija tijekom 3. i 4. stoljeća bila jedno od središta kršćanstva.

U gradu je djelovala **aleksandrijska teološka škola**, u kojoj je odgojen i mladi Atanazije. Ta će ga formacija pratiti kroz cijeli život. Kasnije će se, kako voditelj ističe, upravo na nauk aleksandrijske škole oslanjati kada bude branio božanstvo Krista i Duha Svetoga.
sections.subtitle_en: Child of Alexandria and Its Theological School
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about the birth of St. Athanasius in Alexandria
sections.content_en:
Athanasius was born in **Alexandria between 295 and 298**. Don Mladen Parlov explains that Alexandria during the 3rd and 4th centuries was one of the centers of Christianity.

Active in the city was the **Alexandrian theological school**, in which the young Athanasius was also educated. That formation would accompany him throughout his entire life. Later, as the host emphasizes, it was precisely on the teaching of the Alexandrian school that he would rely when defending the divinity of Christ and of the Holy Spirit.

sections.subtitle: Arijeva hereza: kršćanstvo prilagođeno grčkom ukusu
sections.screenshot_description: Don Mladen Parlov objašnjava kako je Arije htio uklopiti kršćansku poruku u grčku filozofiju
sections.content:
Već potkraj 3. stoljeća u Aleksandriji se javlja **arijanizam**. Njegov začetnik bio je svećenik **Arije**. Don Mladen Parlov tumači da je Arije, u biti, htio **inkulturirati kršćansku poruku u grčki misaoni svijet**.

Zato je počeo učiti da postoji samo jedan Bog, pokretač svega, nalik **aristotelovskom nepokretnom pokretaču**. Logos, o čijem utjelovljenju govore Novi zavjet i kršćanska poruka, po Arijevu nauku ne bi bio pravi Bog, jer Bog može biti samo jedan. Logos bi bio **niže, posredničko biće** preko kojega je Bog stvorio svijet i uredio sve što postoji. Bog ga je poslao, on se utjelovio i bio s ljudima, a zatim je uzet u Božju slavu. Možda sjedi i zdesna Bogu, ali mu nije jednak, jer je jedini Bog Bog Otac.

Voditelj naglašava da to nije bila tek izmišljotina jednog svećenika teologa. Ideja o logosu kao drugotnom, nižem biću bila je **vrlo zamamna za grčku kulturu**. U jednom je trenutku taj nauk prihvatilo **gotovo više od 50 posto biskupskih stolica**. Mnogima se činio u skladu s onim što dominantna kultura želi i lako prihvaća.

Pravovjerni biskupi bili su, međutim, uvjereni da je riječ o **izdaji biblijske vjere**. To je, po njima, bila izdaja vjere predane apostolima, koju su apostoli predali svojim nasljednicima biskupima i koja bi trebala prelaziti iz naraštaja u naraštaj **neokrnjena i cjelovita**.
sections.subtitle_en: Arius's Heresy: Christianity Adapted to Greek Taste
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Mladen Parlov explains how Arius wanted to fit the Christian message into Greek philosophy
sections.content_en:
Already toward the end of the 3rd century, **Arianism** appeared in Alexandria. Its originator was the priest **Arius**. Don Mladen Parlov interprets that Arius, in essence, wanted to **inculturate the Christian message into the Greek world of thought**.

Therefore, he began to teach that there is only one God, the mover of all, akin to the **Aristotelian unmoved mover**. The Logos, of whose incarnation the New Testament and the Christian message speak, according to Arius's teaching would not be true God, because God can only be one. The Logos would be a **lower, intermediary being** through whom God created the world and ordered everything that exists. God sent him, he became incarnate and was with people, and then he was taken into God's glory. Perhaps he even sits at the right hand of God, but he is not equal to him, because the only God is God the Father.

The host emphasizes that this was not merely the invention of a single priest-theologian. The idea of the logos as a secondary, lower being was **very enticing to Greek culture**. At one point, that teaching was accepted by **nearly more than 50 percent of episcopal sees**. To many, it seemed in accordance with what the dominant culture desired and readily accepted.

Orthodox bishops were, however, convinced that it was a **betrayal of biblical faith**. That was, in their view, a betrayal of the faith handed down to the apostles, which the apostles handed down to their successors the bishops and which was supposed to pass from generation to generation **unimpaired and whole**.

sections.subtitle: Nicejski koncil i riječ koja je obranila Kristovo božanstvo
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava pojam homoousios i Atanazijevu ulogu na Nicejskom koncilu
sections.content:
Arijanizam je diljem carstva stvorio velike napetosti. Zato je **car Konstantin 325. godine sazvao koncil u Niceji**. Okupilo se nekoliko stotina biskupa. Don Mladen Parlov spominje brojku od oko 380, uz ogradu da u nju nije siguran.

Na koncilu je sudjelovao i **biskup Aleksandar iz Aleksandrije**. Pratio ga je njegov mladi tajnik, **đakon Atanazije**, koji je tako i sam bio sudionik koncila.

Koncil je obranio vjeru u Isusa Krista tako što je u teologiju uveo pojam preuzet iz grčke filozofije: **homoousios**, odnosno **istobitan**. Izrekom da je Isus Krist, druga božanska osoba, istobitan Ocu, koncil je obranio Kristovo božanstvo i osudio arijanizam.

Voditelj ipak upozorava da arijanizam time **nije nestao**, nego je poprimio druge oblike. Konstantin je prijetnjama vlasti pokušao disciplinirati biskupe i samog Arija da prihvate nicejsku formulu i očuvaju jedinstvo vjere. Carevi nakon njega nisu bili teolozi. Pod utjecajem pojedinih biskupa i svećenika ponovno su podržavali arijanizam, negdje prikriveno, a negdje otvoreno, i time ponovno stvarali probleme Crkvi 4. stoljeća.
sections.subtitle_en: The Council of Nicaea and the Word That Defended Christ's Divinity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the concept of homoousios and Athanasius's role at the Council of Nicaea
sections.content_en:
Arianism created great tensions throughout the empire. Therefore, **Emperor Constantine in 325 convened a council in Nicaea**. Several hundred bishops gathered. Don Mladen Parlov mentions the figure of about 380, with the caveat that he is not certain about it.

Participating in the council was also **Bishop Alexander of Alexandria**. Accompanying him was his young secretary, **Deacon Athanasius**, who was thus himself a participant in the council.

The council defended faith in Jesus Christ by introducing into theology a term borrowed from Greek philosophy: **homoousios**, that is, **consubstantial**. By the statement that Jesus Christ, the second divine person, is consubstantial with the Father, the council defended Christ's divinity and condemned Arianism.

The host nevertheless warns that Arianism thereby **did not disappear**, but assumed other forms. Constantine attempted, through threats of authority, to discipline the bishops and Arius himself to accept the Nicene formula and preserve the unity of faith. The emperors after him were not theologians. Under the influence of particular bishops and priests, they again supported Arianism, in some places covertly, and in others openly, and thereby again created problems for the Church of the 4th century.

sections.subtitle: Najžešći branitelj pravovjerja i biskup pet progonstava
sections.screenshot_description: Don Mladen Parlov govori o Atanazijevim progonstvima i 17 godina provedenih u izgnanstvu
sections.content:
U složenim političkim i društvenim prilikama koje su uslijedile, Atanazije postaje, kako ističe don Mladen Parlov, **najveći branitelj nicejske formule**, izraza homoousios i nicejskog pravovjerja. Voditelj ga naziva „prvakom“ te najvećim i najžešćim braniteljem pravovjerja u prvim desetljećima 4. stoljeća. Bilo je to vrijeme kada se cijelo društvo lomilo oko pitanja Kristove istobitnosti, njegova božanstva i božanskog sinovstva.

Atanazije je **328. godine postao biskup Aleksandrije** i bio je na čelu aleksandrijske Crkve gotovo pola stoljeća. Obrana vjere donijela mu je teške udarce:
- **pet puta** su ga razni carevi i carice slali u progonstvo,
- u progonstvu je ukupno proveo **17 godina**.

Don Mladen Parlov naglašava da su ta progonstva uvijek bila plod dogovora politike i Atanazijevih protivnika. Uz to dodaje kritičku primjedbu: „Nije dobro kad se politika miješa u pitanje vjere, ali tako je bilo onda, tako je nažalost do dana današnjega.“
sections.subtitle_en: The Fiercest Defender of Orthodoxy and Bishop of Five Exiles
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Mladen Parlov speaks about Athanasius's exiles and 17 years spent in banishment
sections.content_en:
In the complex political and social circumstances that ensued, Athanasius became, as Don Mladen Parlov points out, the **greatest defender of the Nicene formula**, of the term homoousios, and of Nicene orthodoxy. The host calls him a “champion” and the greatest and fiercest defender of orthodoxy in the first decades of the 4th century. It was a time when the whole of society was fractured over the question of Christ's consubstantiality, his divinity, and his divine sonship.

Athanasius **became Bishop of Alexandria in 328** and was at the head of the Alexandrian Church for nearly half a century. The defense of the faith brought him heavy blows:
- **five times** various emperors and empresses sent him into exile,
- he spent a total of **17 years** in exile.

Don Mladen Parlov emphasizes that these exiles were always the fruit of agreements between politics and Athanasius's opponents. In addition, he adds a critical remark: “It is not good when politics interferes in matters of faith, but that is how it was then, and that is unfortunately how it is to this very day.”

sections.subtitle: Protiv Arija, o utjelovljenju Riječi i nova zamka polu-arijanizma
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava razliku između homoousios i homoiousios
sections.content:
Atanazijeva teologija vrti se ponajprije oko **obrane božanstva Isusa Krista**. Tome su posvećeni njegovi **spisi protiv Arija**. Kao njegov najvažniji teološki spis don Mladen Parlov izdvaja djelo **„O utjelovljenju Riječi“** (o utjelovljenju logosa). U njemu Atanazije brani nicejsku vjeroispovijest i na temelju Svetoga pisma i teologije dokazuje zašto je logos istobitan Ocu.

Nakon osude arijanizma razvio se pokret **polu-arijanizma**. On je učio da Sin nije *homoousios*, istobitan, nego *homoiousios*, **sličan Ocu**. Voditelj objašnjava da su njegovi zagovornici time htjeli prikriti svoju herezu. Na taj novi i zavodljivi nauk ponovno je pristao velik dio nositelja političke vlasti, careva i carica, što je opet izazvalo probleme u Crkvi 4. stoljeća.

Atanazije je i tada ostao **na braniku pravovjerja**. Nije se ustručavao suprotstaviti carevima i caricama, odlaziti u progonstva te podnositi velike nepravde i udarce zbog obrane istinske vjere.
sections.subtitle_en: Against Arius, On the Incarnation of the Word, and the New Trap of Semi-Arianism
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the difference between homoousios and homoiousios
sections.content_en:
Athanasius's theology revolves primarily around the **defense of the divinity of Jesus Christ**. Dedicated to this are his **writings against Arius**. As his most important theological treatise, Don Mladen Parlov singles out the work **“On the Incarnation of the Word”** (on the incarnation of the logos). In it, Athanasius defends the Nicene creed and, on the basis of Sacred Scripture and theology, proves why the logos is consubstantial with the Father.

Following the condemnation of Arianism, the movement of **Semi-Arianism** developed. It taught that the Son is not *homoousios*, consubstantial, but *homoiousios*, **similar to the Father**. The host explains that its proponents thereby wanted to conceal their heresy. A large portion of political power-holders, emperors, and empresses once again accepted this new and seductive teaching, which again caused problems in the Church of the 4th century.

Athanasius remained even then **on the ramparts of orthodoxy**. He did not hesitate to oppose emperors and empresses, to go into exiles, and to endure great injustices and blows for the defense of the true faith.
keywords_en: On the Incarnation of the Word

sections.subtitle: I Duh Sveti je Bog: pisma Serapionu
sections.screenshot_description: Don Mladen Parlov predstavlja hrvatski prijevod četiri pisma Serapionu
sections.content:
Polu-arijanci, koje don Mladen Parlov naziva i **homejcima** ili semi-arijancima, svojim su naukom osporili i **božanstvo Duha Svetoga**. Zato se Atanazije, nakon obrane Kristova božanstva, u svojim spisima bori i za božanstvo trećeg lica Presvetog Trojstva.

Voditelj posebno ističe da na hrvatskom postoji prijevod njegovih **četiriju pisama Serapionu o Kristu i Duhu**. U tim pismima Atanazije dokazuje božanstvo Isusa Krista i Duha Svetoga. Pritom se oslanja na:
- dobro poznavanje **Svetoga pisma**,
- nauk **aleksandrijske teološke škole**,
- ponajprije **soteriološke razloge**, odnosno razloge vezane uz spasenje.
sections.subtitle_en: The Holy Spirit Is Also God: Letters to Serapion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Mladen Parlov presents the Croatian translation of the four letters to Serapion
sections.content_en:
The Semi-Arians, whom Don Mladen Parlov also calls **Homoians** or semi-Arians, by their teaching also contested the **divinity of the Holy Spirit**. Therefore, Athanasius, after defending Christ's divinity, also fought in his writings for the divinity of the third person of the Most Holy Trinity.

The host especially emphasizes that there is a Croatian translation of his **four letters to Serapion on Christ and the Spirit**. In these letters, Athanasius proves the divinity of Jesus Christ and of the Holy Spirit. In doing so, he relies on:
- a good knowledge of **Sacred Scripture**,
- the teaching of the **Alexandrian theological school**,
- above all **soteriological reasons**, that is, reasons related to salvation.

sections.subtitle: Theosis: Bog je postao čovjekom da bi čovjek bio pobožanstvenjen
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači pojam theosis kao temelj Atanazijeve teologije i duhovnosti
sections.content:
Don Mladen Parlov Atanazijevu argumentaciju sažima u jednostavnu misao: **ako logos nije Bog, ljudi nisu spašeni**. Ako logos koji je postao čovjekom nije Bog, i ako Duh Sveti, koji vjernike sjedinjuje s Isusom Kristom, nije Bog, onda čovjek nije spašen niti pobožanstvenjen.

Temeljni pojam te teologije, koji se kasnije odražava i u duhovnosti koju Atanazije predlaže, jest **theosis**, odnosno **pobožanstvenjenje** ili obogotvorenje. Voditelj ga objašnjava ovako: Krist, Sin Božji, postao je Sin čovječji, jedan od nas, **„da nas učini bogovima, da nas pobožanstveni“**.

To djelo pobožanstvenjenja u čovjeku izvodi Duh Sveti, koji je darovan vjernicima i sjedinjuje ih s Kristom. Upravo je to djelo, zaključuje don Mladen Parlov, **dokaz da je Duh Sveti na strani Stvoritelja, a ne stvorenja**. I logos i Duh Sveti su Bog, a ne posrednička bića ili stvorenja.
sections.subtitle_en: Theosis: God Became Man So That Man Might Be Divinized
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the concept of theosis as the foundation of Athanasius's theology and spirituality
sections.content_en:
Don Mladen Parlov summarizes Athanasius's argumentation into a simple thought: **if the logos is not God, human beings are not saved**. If the logos who became man is not God, and if the Holy Spirit, who unites believers with Jesus Christ, is not God, then man is neither saved nor divinized.

The fundamental concept of that theology, which is later reflected also in the spirituality that Athanasius proposes, is **theosis**, that is, **divinization** or deification. The host explains it like this: Christ, the Son of God, became the Son of Man, one of us, **“to make us gods, to divinize us”**.

That work of divinization in man is accomplished by the Holy Spirit, who is given to believers and unites them with Christ. It is precisely that work, Don Mladen Parlov concludes, that is the **proof that the Holy Spirit is on the side of the Creator, and not of creation**. Both the logos and the Holy Spirit are God, and not intermediary beings or creatures.

sections.subtitle: Život Antuna pustinjaka: mala knjiga koja je pokrenula monaštvo
sections.screenshot_description: Don Mladen Parlov predstavlja spis Vita Antonii i njegov odjek na istoku i zapadu
sections.content:
Važan doprinos duhovnosti istoka i zapada Atanazije je dao malim spisom koji je imao silan odjek: ***Vita Antonii***, odnosno **Život opata Antuna** ili Život Antuna pustinjaka.

U njemu opisuje mladića koji napušta roditeljski dom i povlači se u pustinju. Don Mladen Parlov objašnjava da pustinja tu postaje **bojište Kristova vojnika**. Ondje se onaj tko je izabrao biti vjeran Kristu u samoći i osamljenom životu treba dokazati kao Kristov vojnik.

Atanazije je spis ponio sa sobom u **Trier**, gdje je proveo prvo izgnanstvo. Drugo izgnanstvo proveo je u **Rimu**, gdje se susreo s papom. Papa mu je dao podršku i kasnije pomogao da se vrati na aleksandrijsku stolicu. Kada je životopis preveden na latinski, dao je **snažan impuls zapadnom monaštvu**. Monaštvo je na zapadu već postojalo, u Galiji, oko Akvileje, pa i u okolici carskog grada Triera, ali je ovaj spis donio novi poticaj.

Voditelj smatra da nije nemoguće da je i **sveti Jeronim** upravo čitajući ovaj spis poželio monaški život i povlačenje u osamu. Spis je utjecao i na razvoj **pustinjačkog monaštva u Egiptu**. Takav je život iskusio i sam Atanazije: treće, četvrto i peto progonstvo proveo je **u egipatskoj pustinji među pustinjskim monasima**.
sections.subtitle_en: Life of Anthony the Hermit: The Little Book That Launched Monasticism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Mladen Parlov presents the work Vita Antonii and its resonance in the East and West
sections.content_en:
An important contribution to the spirituality of the East and West was made by Athanasius through a small treatise that had an immense resonance: ***Vita Antonii***, that is, the **Life of Abbot Anthony** or Life of Anthony the Hermit.

In it he describes a young man who leaves his parental home and withdraws into the desert. Don Mladen Parlov explains that the desert here becomes the **battlefield of the soldier of Christ**. There, the one who has chosen to be faithful to Christ in solitude and a solitary life must prove himself as a soldier of Christ.

Athanasius took the writing with him to **Trier**, where he spent his first exile. His second exile he spent in **Rome**, where he met with the Pope. The Pope gave him support and later helped him return to the Alexandrian see. When the biography was translated into Latin, it gave a **strong impulse to Western monasticism**. Monasticism already existed in the West, in Gaul, around Aquileia, and even in the vicinity of the imperial city of Trier, but this treatise brought a new impetus.

The host considers that it is not impossible that **Saint Jerome** also, precisely through reading this treatise, desired monastic life and withdrawal into solitude. The treatise also influenced the development of **eremitic monasticism in Egypt**. Such a life was experienced by Athanasius himself: he spent the third, fourth, and fifth exiles **in the Egyptian desert among the desert monks**.

sections.subtitle: Atanazije protiv svijeta: vjera vrijedna svake žrtve
sections.content:
Zaključujući prikaz, don Mladen Parlov ističe da Atanazije, obiljem svojih spisa i svojim pravovjerjem, svjedoči da **nema žrtve koju ne bi trebalo podnijeti u obrani istinske vjere**. Vjera je tako veliko blago da je vrijedna svake žrtve, čak i žrtve života.

Voditelj podsjeća na poznatu izreku: **„Atanazije protiv svijeta“**. Atanazije se nije bojao progona. Nije se bojao usprotiviti carevima, caricama, političkim moćnicima ni drugim biskupima. Svatko tko nije bio na liniji prave vjere na neki je način bio njegov protivnik.

Don Mladen Parlov odmah pojašnjava da to ne znači da je Atanazije svoje protivnike mrzio, nego da **nije odstupao od istine**.
sections.subtitle_en: Athanasius Against the World: Faith Worth Every Sacrifice
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host quotes the saying “Athanasius against the world”
sections.content_en:
Concluding the presentation, Don Mladen Parlov points out that Athanasius, through the abundance of his writings and his orthodoxy, testifies that **there is no sacrifice that should not be made in defense of the true faith**. The faith is such a great treasure that it is worth every sacrifice, even the sacrifice of life.

The host recalls the famous saying: **“Athanasius against the world”**. Athanasius was not afraid of persecution. He was not afraid to oppose emperors, empresses, political rulers, or other bishops. Everyone who was not on the line of the true faith was in some way his opponent.

Don Mladen Parlov immediately clarifies that this does not mean that Athanasius hated his opponents, but that **he did not deviate from the truth**.

sections.subtitle: Istina ima ime: Atanazijeva poruka u doba relativizma
sections.screenshot_description: Don Mladen Parlov govori o aktualnosti Atanazijeve poruke u svijetu relativizma
sections.content:
Don Mladen Parlov naglašava da je Atanazijeva poruka **vrlo aktualna i izazovna** u današnjem svijetu. To je svijet **relativizma vrednota** i pluralizma ponuda, svijet koji poznaje različita mišljenja i relativizira sve, u kojem svatko ima pravo na vlastitu istinu. Kritički primjećuje da se i s usana suvremenih apostolskih nasljednika, katoličkih biskupa, zna čuti da je kršćanstvo samo jedna od ponuda.

Nasuprot tome, voditelj ističe: **„Za nas kršćane istina ima ime, ona je Isus Krist i ona nam je darovana.“** Kršćani tu istinu primaju sa zahvalnošću i poniznošću i dopuštaju joj da preobražava njihove živote. Kada su je primili, ne žele je zadržati za sebe. Poput Atanazija žele svjedočiti da je istina objavljena u Isusu Kristu **jedina koja može do kraja osmisliti i ostvariti ljudski život** i dovesti u život vječni.

Osjećaj duboke zahvalnosti, prema riječima don Mladena Parlova, obvezuje kršćane da tu istinu svjedoče pred cijelim svijetom: da je Isus Krist **jedini put, jedina istina i jedini život**.

Epizodu zaključuje molitvenom željom da, po Atanazijevu primjeru, i suvremeni kršćani dođu do uvjerenja kako ne postoji ništa tako veliko kao **blago vjere**, vrijedno svake žrtve, „ne dao Bog, čak i žrtve života“. Oproštaj je isti kao i pozdrav na početku: „Hvaljen Isus i Marija.“
sections.subtitle_en: Truth Has a Name: Athanasius's Message in an Age of Relativism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Don Mladen Parlov speaks about the relevance of Athanasius's message in a world of relativism
sections.content_en:
Don Mladen Parlov emphasizes that Athanasius's message is **very timely and challenging** in today's world. It is a world of **relativism of values** and pluralism of offers, a world that knows different opinions and relativizes everything, in which everyone has the right to their own truth. He critically notes that even from the lips of modern apostolic successors, Catholic bishops, one can hear that Christianity is merely one among offerings.

In contrast to this, the host emphasizes: **“For us Christians, truth has a name, it is Jesus Christ and it has been given to us as a gift.”** Christians receive that truth with gratitude and humility and allow it to transform their lives. When they have received it, they do not want to keep it to themselves. Like Athanasius, they want to testify that the truth revealed in Jesus Christ is the **only one that can fully give meaning to and fulfill human life** and lead into eternal life.

A feeling of deep gratitude, according to the words of Don Mladen Parlov, obliges Christians to testify to that truth before the entire world: that Jesus Christ is **the only way, the only truth, and the only life**.

He concludes the episode with a prayerful wish that, following Athanasius's example, contemporary Christians may also come to the conviction that there is nothing so great as the **treasure of faith**, worthy of every sacrifice, “God forbid, even the sacrifice of life”. The farewell is the same as the greeting at the beginning: “Praised be Jesus and Mary.”
